text:
ashwin: FYI starting a preflight for AcmeCorp POC (Private deployment). They want L4 edge proxy + active/passive failover to our dedicated pool. Need a checklist for network rules and failover behavior. Any blockers?

beth (sales-eng): Quick Q — customer wants NAT from on-prem -> our PrivateLink? Or will we terminate in their VPC and call back? They mentioned egress through corp proxy.

maria (netops): We need their CIDR for peering + list of IPs to allow to the PrivateLink endpoint. Also confirm if they need AWS PrivateLink or Transit Gateway peering. TGW preferred for large prefixes.

alex (eng): For PrivateLink option we'll supply a service endpoint. Required outbound from customer: 443 to service IPs we allocate (we usually allocate 10.250.0.0/28 per region). If using peering/TGW then must allow 10.244.0.0/21 -> our subnets. Healthcheck ports: TCP 443 and TCP 2200 (control plane) — include both.

sean (solutions): POC duration is 4 weeks; pricing for private endpoints during POC is blended, will send the note. Also they require mTLS? Customer answer?

beth (sales-eng): @ashwin they said they prefer TLS passthrough at L4 and app handles TLS. No mTLS initially.

maria (netops): Firewall rules I'd request:
- allow outbound 443 to 10.250.0.0/28 (our PrivateLink VIPs)
- allow outbound 2200 to 10.250.0.0/28 for control plane
- NTP (UDP 123) to 0.0.0.0/0 or internal NTP
- DNS outbound UDP/TCP 53 to their resolver
Also ensure asymmetric routing not blocked for return traffic.

alex (eng): If they do TGW/peering we need to reserve a /27 for our ENIs. Also ensure no SNAT on their side for return path if they want client source IP preserved. For failover we use BGP community to prefer primary region, announce secondary when primary unhealthy. If they can't run BGP we can do active/passive with healthcheck-driven route failover via IP failover (requires support from their infra).

ashwin: Can you put that into a firewall snippet I can send in the security questionnaire? Also we need an estimated egress bandwidth for pricing — they said ~300 Mbps sustained.

netops-bot: deploy-checklist triggered by @maria
- Required: CIDR, preferred connectivity type (privatelink/tgw), firewall snippet, peering acl
- Optional: BGP ASNs for failover
Status: checklist created (ID 9876)

maria (netops): snippet for SQA:

```
Allow outbound:
- TCP 443 -> 10.250.0.0/28 (Redwood PrivateLink)
- TCP 2200 -> 10.250.0.0/28 (control plane)
- UDP 123 -> customer NTP pool
- UDP/TCP 53 -> customer DNS
Notes:
- Ensure return path allowed; avoid forced SNAT on egress for IP preservation.
- If using TGW/peering, permit inbound from 10.244.0.0/21 to customer app subnets.
```

beth (sales-eng): Perfect. I'll paste that into the SQA and flag the billing note. @sean can you send the POC pricing for 300 Mbps + two regions failover?

sean (solutions): On it, will DM pricing and include optional BGP setup cost. Also will ask legal for SLA carveout for POC.

ashwin: Thanks — can we also confirm their on-prem firewall vendor? Palo Alto or Forti? If Palo we can give an XML snippet.

maria (netops): They said Palo Alto. I'll add a PAN-OS security rule later if you need it.

ashwin: Great. Closing on this thread — will update when they return CIDR and ASN.
